$comment: AFLDB-ISSUE-093 — canonical acceptance/promotion register for fitzRoy core snapshots.
This file records that a specific set of IMMUTABLE raw artefacts, under a specific
importer/contract version, passed INDEPENDENT full-history validation and is accepted
as the rebuild's canonical core source. It is a promotion record, not evidence: the
acquisition manifests under docs/rebuild-manifests/afltables_fitzroy_core/ remain
untouched historical evidence and are never rewritten to reflect an acceptance.
This file is NOT sufficient to bless bytes. Hand-editing it cannot make a snapshot
acceptable, because tools/migration/import_fitzroy_core.py re-derives every
full-history gate from the contract and the artefacts on disk, re-verifies every
artefact SHA-256 against the acquisition manifest, and remains the sole verdict
authority. What this file adds is BINDING: it pins which acquisition is accepted, and
the hashes and measured fingerprints that must still hold for it to stay accepted.
The acquisition manifest's own `full_history` and `completeness` fields are INERT.
full-history-20260827 self-declared full_history=true while the independent validator
rejected it (the acquirer implemented a smaller gate set than the contract declares).
That manifest is preserved byte-for-byte as the record of that mistake.
The rebuild resolves its default core source by selecting the single entry whose
acceptance_status is 'accepted'. Zero accepted entries and more than one accepted
entry are BOTH refusals. There is no 'latest label', filename-ordering or date
tiebreak: deterministic selection among multiple baselines is not defined policy,
so the rebuild fails closed and a human must decide.
Never read as a verdict by any part of the supported rebuild path. They are the
acquirer's self-assessment, preserved for audit only.
manifest_sha256 covers the acquisition manifest byte-for-byte, so the artefact
hash list inside it cannot be edited to cover for a tampered artefact without
breaking this binding.

raw_artefacts.digest_rule: sha256 over sorted lines '<filename> <sha256> <row_count>\n' from the acquisition manifest's files[]
$comment: A second, independently recomputable binding to the same artefact set. It survives
insignificant reformatting of the manifest while still pinning every filename,
content hash and row count.
The verdict recorded here is history. Every normal rebuild re-runs this exact
command in PRECHECK, before any destructive stage, and uses that live result.

measured.$comment: Drift gates. Re-derived from the snapshot on every validate and compared exactly.

$comment: Canonical identity is the AFL Tables profile URL. The fitzRoy numeric ID is
optional: 83 recent-2025 rows carry none, and distinct_urls - distinct_ids = 5
is exactly the five players who have no ID anywhere in the snapshot.
Settled under contract_version 1. Each is tracked in fitzroy-contract.json or
pinned in the importer; this list states what the acceptance covers, and a change
to any of them is a new acceptance decision, not an edit to this one.

source_data.rule: two spurious 1909 Jim Stewart Cartesian-product rows dropped under tracked row fingerprints

import_transformation.rule: blank Player falls back to First.name + ' ' + Surname only when both are present; a non-blank Player always wins; neither present still fails closed
